clue.text: Attractive tailless insect approaching

indicators.note: without a tail, the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A pretty bug with no tail creeps closer.
explanation.walkthrough: BEE without its last letter gives BE, followed by COMING to make BECOMING.
explanation.definitionFit: A becoming outfit is one that flatters the wearer and looks good on them.

clue.text: Aristocrat open-minded at first visiting London borough

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so one piece enters another

parts.note: Barnet is a borough in north London

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A liberal-thinking nobleman drops in on a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open-minded' looks like it describes the aristocrat, but only its opening letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British title ranking below a baron, so is one of the titled class.

clue.text: Clutched cold body part

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone gripped a chilly part of their body.
explanation.definitionFit: Clung is the past tense of cling, meaning held on tightly.

clue.text: CID men liable to break training equipment

indicators.note: to break means to smash apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Detectives are expected to smash up the gym kit.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine ball is a heavy weighted ball thrown and caught in fitness exercises.

clue.text: Almost time when stars are visible

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It is nearly the hour when the stars come out.
explanation.definitionFit: After sunset, in darkness, the sky shows its stars, which is the dark period between evenings and mornings.

clue.text: When initially in space, stare open-mouthed

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another
initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A puzzled astronaut gazes around the void with jaw dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside GAP to make GAWP.
explanation.definitionFit: Gawp is a British informal verb for gazing stupidly, mouth hanging, at something.

clue.text: Difficult week, Grant admits

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: WK is the abbreviation for week

explanation.surface: Someone called Grant confesses to a tough seven days.
explanation.walkthrough: Grant looks like a name, but it is the noun for money given; WK goes in after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means hard to deal with or causing trouble and embarrassment.

clue.text: Contribution to hardship in Chelmsford nick

indicators.note: a contribution is a part, so the letters come from inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of hardship, in, and the start of Chelmsford

explanation.surface: Someone donates to relieve poverty in an Essex town's police station.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelmsford is the county town of Essex; nick is British slang for a police station, but here it means to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick and pinch are both British slang verbs meaning to steal something.

clue.text: Months ago, trainees resolved situation with three involved

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for months

indicators.note: resolved means broken down and reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: Some time back, apprentices settled an awkward three-way arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A ménage à trois is a domestic or romantic arrangement involving three people living together.

clue.text: Ignoring its tip, earth's spherical

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, which is ignored and dropped

parts.note: earth as soil or land is ground

explanation.surface: Someone observes that the planet, viewed without its top, is a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: GROUND loses its G to leave ROUND; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaped like a ball or globe is described as being round.

clue.text: That woman's family is after good food to pickle

indicators.note: is after places the family piece behind the other piece

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
the possessive pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: Her relatives are hunting for good things to preserve in vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: A gherkin is a small cucumber, typically preserved in vinegar as a pickle.

clue.text: Badger or horse?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pester someone repeatedly
second meaning: an old or worn-out horse

explanation.walkthrough: The question pretends to ask which animal is meant, but Badger is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for persistent pestering and as a noun for an elderly, tired steed.

clue.text: Chopped down tree has striking appearance

explanation.surface: A felled tree makes an impressive sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped down' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a dash is an idiom meaning to look stylish and impressive.

clue.text: Group of workers search engine pipes?

explanation.surface: A union wonders whether a search engine could pipe things through.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'pipes' is a plural noun standing for a mass noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubing is a length or collection of tubes, which is to say pipes in general.

clue.text: Raised details intended to make Reading more accessible?

definitions.text: Raised details intended to make Reading more accessible?

parts.words: Raised details intended to make Reading more accessible?
parts.note: surface reading: an architectural or civic feature to help people get around the town of Reading in Berkshire
setter's reading: patterns of embossed dots that let blind people read by touch

explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Reading look like the English town; it is simply reading text.
explanation.definitionFit: The tactile script of raised dots devised by Louis Braille lets visually impaired people read with fingertips.

clue.text: Marshy area ahead of the German guard

indicators.note: ahead of puts the marsh piece in front of what follows

parts.note: der is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A German sentry patrols in front of a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A fender is a protective barrier, such as the metal guard in front of a fireplace.

clue.text: Flexible like part of bridge?

definitions.note: a playful adjective formed from the noun rubber
definitions.meaning: second meaning: resembling a rubber, a set of games in the card game bridge

explanation.walkthrough: Bridge suggests a structure over a river, but it is the card game, where a rubber is a best-of-three set.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbery describes an elastic, springy texture, and whimsically means resembling a rubber at cards.

clue.text: Most despicable taxi drivers blocking street

indicators.note: something blocking a road sits within it, so one piece lies inside the other

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Nasty taxi drivers have parked across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most despicable taxi drivers' reads as one phrase about bad cabbies; the definition stops after the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabby is an informal word for mean or contemptible, so the superlative is lowest of all.

clue.text: Tease American about sweetener in tea?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the pieces are read from the end backwards

explanation.surface: Someone teases an American about what goes in his cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that tea is only one place the sweetener goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is the common sweetening substance many people stir into a cup.

clue.text: Making a comeback, survive hard period

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word is read going back the other way

parts.note: to cope is to manage or survive
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A sportsman bouncing back endures a tough spell.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is an era or long stretch of time marked by particular events.

clue.text: Biblical character's task

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the patient sufferer of the Old Testament book
second meaning: a piece of work to be done

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive linking the two, but it is just 'is'; the same letters are pronounced differently in each sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament man Job shares his spelling with the common word for a chore or piece of work.

clue.text: Drink most of pitcher — very cold water

indicators.note: most of means all but a bit, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone downs nearly a whole jug of icy water.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice is a beverage made from the liquid squeezed out of fruit.

clue.text: Famous Italian goalie tumbles across line

indicators.note: across has the goalkeeper sprawled over the line, holding it within
tumbles means falls in a heap, mixing the letters up

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An Italian keeper dives full length over the goal line.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the celebrated Italian astronomer and physicist of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Old French wine, the ultimate for entrée like lamb?

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: the ultimate is the very last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A menu suggests an aged French wine with the main course, perhaps lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks lamb as just one example of a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means relating to sheep, and lamb is the young of that animal.

clue.text: Regretted offensive broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means transmitted over the air, so we hear the word spoken

explanation.surface: A broadcaster is sorry for an offensive programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to feel sorrow or remorse about it, so rued is past tense.

clue.text: Manufactured clash, yet in a restrained way

indicators.note: something manufactured is assembled from parts, so the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: A staged confrontation was nonetheless played out with restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting chastely means acting modestly and with self-control, especially avoiding indulgence.
